REUTERS Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save KISVARDA, Hungary/GDANSK, Poland (Reuters) — Facing a choice between upsetting businesses and a public opinion backlash, the Polish and Hungarian ruling centrists are opting ​for curbs on foreign labor — something economists warn may hurt the two countries' growth prospects. Both Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar, who won in a landslide ‌in April, and his Polish counterpart Donald Tusk, in power since 2023, have been painted by their nationalist rivals as soft on immigration. Now, both are taking action to prove them wrong. Tusk's government slashed work permits for non-EU citizens by 22% last year, while Hungary's new government in June stopped issuing worker visas to employees from the Philippines, Georgia and Armenia, calling it a first step towards regulating guest workers. Public opinion ​polls show broad support for such curbs. In Poland, around two-thirds of respondents in an IBRiS survey for Wirtualna Polska news website in January said Poland ​should accept fewer non-EU migrants. In Hungary, an analysis published by Republikon Institute earlier this month showed that almost half of Hungarians would ⁠not allow any migrants from poorer countries and another 40% only a smaller number. That contrasts with what economists and business groups say both countries badly need. "Fewer workers mean slower ​growth and less tax coming in, while an older population costs more in pensions and health," said Marcin Tomaszewski, lead economist for the EU region at the European Bank for Reconstruction ​and Development, who noted Poland and Hungary face steeper challenges than Western Europe. "Both are aging before they are rich, and both only recently became places people move to rather than leave," he said. The Polish Economic Institute forecast in 2024 that Poland, whose labor force already relies on over 1 million foreigners, around two-thirds of whom are Ukrainian, could have 2.1 million fewer workers by 2035, with declines in industry ​alone potentially knocking 6% to 8% off gross domestic product. A 2026 report by Deloitte, Ipsos and the Institute of Public Affairs, showed non-EU workers contributing up to 10.7% of Poland's ​economic output last year amid birth rates which are at their lowest since World War II. Warsaw says, however, that reconciling employers' needs and transitioning from being a source of migration to hosting non-European ‌migration is ⁠a fine balancing act. "If we changed our status from typical emigration country to migration one, we have to also adjust our whole system of functioning of the society," Polish Deputy Interior Minister Maciej Duszczyk told Reuters, adding that Poland did not want an economy based largely on “cheap labor.” In June, the ministry said it had issued eight times fewer work visas in the first quarter of 2026 compared to the same period in 2022, though that comparison was affected by a change in rules for Ukrainians. Political storm In Hungary, Magyar, whose pro-European course ​and promise to break with Viktor Orban's crony ​capitalism were welcomed by investors, found ⁠himself embroiled in a public spat with one Hungarian business, which said it might halt a factory expansion because of the new migration policies. Magyar accused the Master Good poultry producer, which had received state support, of trying to "threaten the government and the Hungarian people," and said ​it could hire locally if it paid more. Owner Laszlo Barany, however, argued his 580 Filipino staff was essential given an aging ​population. "People get old, they retire ⁠and there is no demographic supply, while those entering the workforce are not looking for this type of job," he said. In Poland, businesses complain about long processing times, with work permits taking over six months and residence permit applications taking nearly a year to process, said Nadia Winiarska, deputy director of the labor department at Polish business federation Lewiatan. While Duszczyk said the visa system ⁠was being ​updated, business owners warn skilled workers could be heading elsewhere. Rahul Jha, a 35-year-old restaurant owner, said he lost ​a chef at his South Indian restaurant who got tired after waiting for over a year for a temporary residence permit. "Denmark gave him a five-year visa ... like immediately, a skilled visa. So he just moved out from ​here." https://www.salon.com/2026/07/25/andrew-.text: analysis Andrew Tate’s arrest causes trouble for Trump’s youngest son The manosphere influencer has lost the president's support — but he could pose a threat to Barron By Sophia Tesfaye Senior Writer Published July 25, 2026 6:45AM (EDT) Barron Trump has defended Andrew Tate against allegations of sex trafficking (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images) Facebook X Reddit Email Save The shift was as swift as it was cold. Standing before reporters in the briefing room on Thursday, White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt was asked a direct question: Would President Donald Trump or his administration intervene to stop the extradition of Andrew and Tristan Tate to the United Kingdom on 59 charges of rape, sex trafficking, assault and extreme pornography? Her single-word response — “No” — denied the brothers, who have been championed by many MAGA media figures as examples of white male persecution, a lifeline. On Thursday, federal marshals in Miami took the Tates into custody . In addition to the charges they face in the U.K., the brothers remain embroiled in grave human-trafficking and minor-exploitation proceedings in Romania and investigations in Florida about new allegations. In the days since their arrest, their attorney Joseph McBride — who has also represented Jan. 6 defendants — has insisted the arrest is political persecution, and he has been amplifying supportive commentary online from media figures with close ties to the Trump administration. MAGA influencer and white nationalist Nick Fuentes wrote that it would be a “national humiliation” if Trump agreed to extradite the brothers to Britain over what he called “trumped up ‘Me Too’ charges.” Other far-right influencers reportedly joined in , but to no avail. For years, the brothers were treated by the MAGA ecosystem not as alleged traffickers facing serious criminal scrutiny, but as useful avatars of male grievance and anti-feminist rebellion. Trump’s refusal to intervene in the Tates’ extradition fight is a much-delayed correction. For years, the brothers were treated by the MAGA ecosystem not as alleged traffickers facing serious criminal scrutiny, but as useful avatars of male grievance and anti-feminist rebellion. That bargain is now boomeranging in the direction of a different Trump: Barron. The key to understanding how the Tate brothers rose to such political heights — and why their collapse now threatens to drag the president’s youngest son into a potentially damaging congressional spotlight — can be found in the conservative media ecosystem that laundered Andrew Tate into a right-wing icon. When mainstream platforms like YouTube, Meta and TikTok finally moved to deplatform the Tate brothers in 2022, the right-wing media apparatus stepped in to grant Tate a second — and far more dangerous — life. Tucker Carlson first gave Tate a platform on Fox News back in 2022 and later hosted a long, sympathetic interview. Elon Musk reinstated Tate’s X account, restoring his reach to over 11 million followers while repeatedly tweeting defenses that hand-waved sex trafficking allegations as political distractions. The late Charlie Kirk chimed in on behalf of Tate: “What he says is so powerful. Our society is configured towards collapsing the American man.” MAGA podcaster Candace Owens dedicated hours of airtime to declaring the Tates’ innocence while launching vicious smear campaigns against their victims. The brothers were indicted in Romania in 2023 on charges of rape and human trafficking, accused of running a criminal operation that lured women — including, prosecutors allege, a 17-year-old — into pornography and prostitution. But in February 2025, weeks after Trump’s second inauguration, Romanian authorities lifted the travel restrictions that had kept the Tates in the country, and the pair immediately boarded a private jet to Florida. At the time, the country’s foreign minister Emil Hurezeanu said that a U.S. official had expressed interest in the case . Trump, for his part, said he knew “nothing about” any pressure his administration might have applied. Related The online clip factory that’s radicalizing teen boys The reporting since then has filled in the blanks. ProPublica reported that federal authorities were told to return electronic devices they had seized from the Tates during an investigation and chided by political appointees like Paul Ingrassia — a vocal Tate defender appointed to the General Services Administration. Heidi Blake, the New Yorker reporter who has covered the Tates more exhaustively than perhaps anyone else, has traced a direct line from a Munich Security Conference conversation between U.S. special envoy Richard Grenell and Hurezeanu to Romanian prosecutors reaching out to the Tates’ lawyers within days, asking what the Americans wanted. Experts labeled the political interference highly inappropriate, but it worked. The travel ban on the brothers was lifted. Within days of Andrew Tate landing back on U.S. soil, another woman came forward accusing him of assault and strangulation — the same pattern of abuse, Blake has said, described by victim after victim in this case. This machinery surrounding was never a secret. What has been less investigated, at least until this week, is how deep the personal relationships ran — specifically, the friendship between Andrew Tate and the president’s 20-year-old son. According to reporting in the New York Times, Tate spoke with Barron Trump over a Zoom call last year with a mutual friend present, and the two discussed their shared belief that the Romanian case against Tate was an effort to silence him. That claim — the idea that a rape and trafficking prosecution amounts to censorship — is the same framing Tate’s MAGA allies have pushed for years. Barron’s older brother, Donald Trump Jr., has called Tate’s 2023 detention “absolute insanity.” Tate publicly boasted about his access to MAGA’s top circles, bragging in 2024 that he was “very close with the Trump family” and that he was looking forward to reminding Donald Trump that he was a “bulletproof bada*s.” Start your day with essential news from Salon. Sign up for our free morning newsletter , Crash Course. For Trump’s presidential campaign, the alliance delivered results. By leveraging the manosphere media network that Tate helped anchor, the campaign mobilized a wave of low-propensity young male voters in 2024. So why did the Trump White House suddenly cut the Tate brothers loose? The breakdown was not sparked by a sudden moral awakening regarding sex trafficking or rape. It was likely sparked by the cardinal sin of the MAGA media universe: political disloyalty. In February, as the administration weighed military action in the Middle East, Andrew Tate took to his livestreaming platform to launch a furious, unhinged tirade against Trump’s strike on Iran. “I do not support war with Iran for Israel,” Tate raged to his audience, accusing the administration of driving the country into disaster while ignoring domestic collapse. “If you’re at home in America right now and you feel like your country is f****d… and moral degeneracy is out of control . . . why would the U.S. going into a war with Iran benefit anybody in America at all? Give me one possible reason. NOBODY WANTS THIS WAR.” For a White House that demands absolute, unyielding fealty, Tate’s high-profile attack was an unpardonable breach. When the British government authorized 38 new criminal charges against the Tates and submitted an updated extradition request to the Justice Department, the White House’s calculation was simple. The political cost of protecting two alleged serial rapists, one of whom was actively attacking the president on foreign policy, far outweighed any remaining value they brought to the youth-culture strategy. The administration threw them to the wolves . While the administration may hope that cutting the Tates loose will close the book on this embarrassing chapter, the fallout from their tangled relationships with the first family and the wider MAGA sphere may just be beginning. Rep.Yassamin Ansari, D-Ariz., has formally urged House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer to open a swift investigation into the Tate brothers’ relationships within Trump’s inner circle. In a searing letter, she highlighted grave diplomatic and ethical concerns regarding whether political networks leveraged their influence to shield accused human traffickers. It doesn’t help the administration’s case that the Tate brothers were, by multiple accounts, still socializing with Trump-world figures in Washington in the days before their arrest. Ansari said she learned only this week that the brothers had traveled to D.C. for meetings, including one with Rep. Wesley Hunt, R-Texas. Our Summer sale is on! Support Salon’s bold journalism. Annual members save 58% The Arizona congresswoman wants the committee to subpoena communications between the Tates and administration officials, and she wants Barron Trump to testify under oath about whether he “influenced official actions or administration policy” about the brothers. There is no evidence that Barron engaged in criminal wrongdoing or played any role in the government’s decisions involving the Tates. But his choice to enthusiastically fraternize with a self-described misogynist facing dozens of horrific felony counts has exposed him to scrutiny. Barron Trump was not an unwitting bystander dragged into a media storm. He was an active participant in defending Andrew Tate, using his influence to validate an accused predator because it fit the edgy, anti-establishment aesthetic of the modern manosphere media. Now, as congressional scrutiny looms and the Tate brothers prepare to face trial in a U.S. federal court before being extradited to London, the president’s youngest son is left facing the stark consequences of his MAGA alliances. Beállítom Levelet írt Gianni Infantinónak, a Nemzetközi Labdarúgó-szövetség (FIFA) elnökének Csányi Sándor, a Magyar Labdarúgó Szövetség (MLSZ) elnöke, és a FIFA alelnöke. Csányi a levélben kemény kritikát fogalmazott meg, és jelezte, a továbbiakban nem tudja támogatni a szövetség vezetőjét, miután az hétfőn kirúgta a FIFA operatív igazgatóját, aki korábban hevesen ellenezte azt a tervezetet, amiben Infantino külső befektetőket vont volna be a FIFA által szervezett tornák lebonyolításába – írja a Bloomberg . A lap által megszerzett levél alapján Csányinál akkor telt be a pohár, amikor a FIFA hétfőn megerősítette, valóban kirúgták Kevin Lamour operatív igazgatót a szövetségtől. A hivatalos közlemény szerint közös megegyezéssel váltak el a felek, de szinte biztos, hogy a háttérben az áll, hogy Lamour korábban az elnök egyszemélyes projektjének nevezte a külső befektetők bevonásáról szóló tervezetet, és azt mondta, a dolog a FIFA vezetését is meglepetésként érte. „A tény, hogy a kirúgásának oka az, hogy ellenezte a tervezetet – amiről utólag végül ön is beismerte, hogy nem volt helyénvaló –, komoly hiányosságokra világít rá az ítélőképességét, az erkölcsi iránytűjét és a vezetői képességeit illetően” – írta Csányi Infantinónak. Az már korábban kiderült, hogy Csányi is elutasítja a tervezett projektet, az MLSZ a 24.hu-nak küldött válaszában azt írta, a magyar szövetség vezetője rendkívül súlyosnak és elfogadhatatlannak tartja , hogy a FIFA-elnök külső befektetőknek akarta eladni a labdarúgó-világbajnokságok kereskedelmi jogainak egy részét. Az MLSZ ügyben képviselt álláspontjáról eddig annyit lehetett tudni, hogy a többi 54 UEFA-taghoz hasonlóan ők is támogatták az európai szövetség bojkottfelhívását, most kiderült, hogy ők is a sajtóból értesültek róla, és amellett, hogy elutasítják, azt is támogatják, hogy az ügyet egy független külső szereplő vizsgálja ki. A FIFA svájci elnöke a nemrég véget ért vb után állt elő azzal az ötlettel, hogy a szövetság egy új leányvállalaton keresztül vonjon be külső befektetőket az általa rendezett versenysorozatok, így a világbajnokságok lebonyolításába is. Infantino a FIFA összes tagszövetségének 40 millió dollárt ajánlott fel a terv támogatásáért, de a tervezet így is nagy botrányt kavart. Az UEFA bojkottal fenyegetett arra az esetre, ha a terv megvalósul, és még a FIFA vezetésén belül is kemény ellenállást váltott ki a dolog. Infantino pár napon belül visszakozott, majd elnézést is kért , ám ekkorra már több szövetség is távozásra szólította fel, sőt még az óriás fociszponzor Carlsberg is erősen utalt arra, hogy ideje lenne lemondania. https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfre.text: Illustration: Anaïs Mims/Getty View image in fullscreen Illustration: Anaïs Mims/Getty Opinion The far right European democracies are running out of time to turn away from the abyss Rafael Behr Far-right parties, Maga ideology and Kremlin money are conniving to suffocate liberal idealism for another generation Wed 9 Sep 2026 01.00 EDT Last modified on Wed 9 Sep 2026 06.08 EDT Share N ot all that long ago, Europe was a beacon of liberal idealism. One memoir recalls it as an era “comfortably saturated with confidence in the unfailing and binding power of tolerance and conciliation”. The economic system seemed obviously preferable to barbarous alternatives. “People honestly believed that the divergencies and the boundaries between nations and sects would gradually melt away into a common humanity,” the author added. Those words could describe the spirit of globalisation at the turn of the millennium. They were written in the 1930s by Stefan Zweig , reflecting on the optimism of late 19th-century Vienna from the perspective of a Jewish émigr é whose world had been destroyed by murderous nationalism. Zweig took his own life in 1942. He never saw fascism defeated. He couldn’t have imagined a renaissance of liberalism in the second half of the 20th century so complete as to attain a pitch of complacency rivalling the one he remembered from his childhood. Now momentum is with the nationalists again. Victory for the Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) in the region of Saxony-Anhalt over the weekend is not the biggest electoral prize won by a far-right party in Europe in recent years, but it is one of the most shocking because it is Germany. No country had more to learn from history if it wanted to immunise its democracy against extremism. None pursued a more systematic programme of inoculation. The word for it is Vergangenheitsbewältigung – hard to say and tricky to translate, meaning roughly coming to terms with a shameful past. There is no excuse of ignorance about the AfD’s rise. It is a knowing repudiation of atonement. The party flirts with Nazi imagery and embraces racist definitions of nationhood, seeking to deport Germans whose credentials it sees as biologically improper. It is extreme enough to induce squeamishness in Marine Le Pen, leader of France’s far-right National Rally (RN). She has spent years carefully cultivating respectability and is leading the polls ahead of next year’s presidential election. She doesn’t want to jeopardise her mainstream credentials by association with the unambiguous extreme. That is less of an impediment across the Atlantic. Elon Musk is an AfD fan , deploying his control of X to boost the party’s campaign messages. Last year, the US vice-president, JD Vance, met Alice Weidel, AfD co-leader, during a visit to Munich. There was no space in his diary for Olaf Scholz, then the German chancellor. Clearly, the AfD meets the criteria for endorsement set out in Donald Trump’s national security strategy , which pledges support for “patriotic resistance” movements committed to halting the “civilisational erasure” of Europe by immigration. In Britain, Nigel Farage could once have assumed entitlement to that status as an early and enthusiastic cheerleader for Trump. But in the competition for Maga accolades, Reform UK has lost ground to parties and people even further to the right – Rupert Lowe’s Restore Britain; ultra-nationalist agitator Tommy Robinson; pretty much anyone who can muster a mob of blackshirts or a passing troll who catches Musk’s eye posting racist conspiracy theories online. 27:02 Rise of the far right: can Farage get a boost from AfD’s win in Germany? | Politics Weekly It would be absurd if it wasn’t so effective. “We never fall into the same abyss twice,” writes Éric Vuillard, the French novelist. “But we fall in the same way, in a mixture of ridicule and dread.” The reach and pungency of the US right, drenched in white supremacism, interferes with Farage’s old strategy of banking far-right support and feinting moderation to make gains in the mainstream. Chasing credibility with fanatical racists in an international digital arena makes it hard to reassure a domestic analogue audience that he should be allowed near Downing Street. The tension shows in Farage’s attitude to the AfD. He spoke at a rally for it in 2017. Now he describes it as a “mixed bag” of a party , whose cultural stances are “utterly respectable and decent” but whose enthusiasm for dictators is “very difficult”. Farage has called AfD support for Vladimir Putin “hard to understand”. It can’t be that far beyond comprehension for a man who, in 2014, described the Russian president as the world leader he most admired , albeit “as an operator, not a human being”. If Farage needs further insight into what might motivate a Kremlin fellow traveller, he could reach out to Reform’s former leader in Wales, Nathan Gill, who is serving a prison sentence for accepting bribes to make pro-Russian speeches in the European parliament when he was a Brexit party MEP. Proximity to the Moscow line is a fairly reliable measure of fanaticism and venality on the spectrum from far-right to even further-right politics in Europe and the US. The same applies on the left, where a credulous appetite for Russian propaganda endures decades after the demise of Soviet ideology. Thankfully, there is not much of a market in British politics for openly pandering to Putin. That is one reason why Trump is also unpopular, although opinion polls suggest he is viewed more favourably by Reform supporters than the wider public. Farage has stopped boasting of his White House connections, perhaps because they have dried up, or maybe because sycophantic flapping around a foreign tyrant, even an American one, doesn’t project strength in a wannabe prime minister. It is striking how little the Reform leader has to say about the rest of the world and Britain’s place in it. The topic was hardly mentioned at the party’s annual conference last week. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Matters of Opinion Guardian columnists and writers on what they’ve been debating, thinking about, reading, and more after newsletter promotion There was a theatrical appearance by Jordan Bardella , the young Le Pen protege and likely prime minister if she wins the presidency. He signed a legally meaningless “deal” with Farage on stopping small-boat traffic across the Channel and was immediately criticised back home for selling out to the UK. The likelihood of a French far-right government taking in more migrants as a policy favour to the UK is close to zero. Having xenophobic nationalists setting the agenda in Paris and London wouldn’t make relations easier, no matter what ideological amity they now claim. As the architect of Brexit, Farage is one of the most consequential politicians of his generation, but he can’t plausibly claim it as an achievement, even when addressing an auditorium of loyal fans. They know it has failed as well as everyone else. A Reform UK without Nigel Farage used to be unthinkable. Not any more | Gaby Hinsliff Read more Farage probably misses the simplicity of his old crusade against Brussels. He might envy nationalist counterparts on the continent, who get to rail against liberal Europeanism while enjoying the economic and strategic privileges afforded by EU membership. They don’t have to explain why it’s so cold on the outside. They play the Eurosceptic game, mobilising the same resentments, targeting the same scapegoats, but modifying the demands in recognition that Farage’s victory was pyrrhic. It doesn’t pay to actually leave. The ambition is to capture the European project, not destroy it, although it amounts to the same thing if the transformation happens through connivance with Maga ideology and Kremlin money. This doesn’t have to be Europe’s destiny. Nationalists do not form a monolithic bloc. The essence of their creed militates against cross-border partnership. Their egos generate more rivalries than alliances. Their selfishness sabotages deals. Countervailing forces can be mustered. There is no law of history that says a height of liberal optimism must be followed by an equivalent fall into chaos. The “binding power of tolerance and conciliation” was not defeated in the 20th century and it won’t be suffocated in this one either. We see the abyss. We can pass without plunging to the bottom. Photograph: Kyle Mazza/Shutterstock New Jersey New Jersey lieutenant governor resigns after sexual harassment accusation Investigation determined Dale Caldwell violated state ethics rules and engaged in harassing behavior Ariana Baio Fri 25 Sep 2026 15.52 EDT First published on Fri 25 Sep 2026 15.12 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Dale Caldwell, the lieutenant governor of New Jersey, resigned from his position on Friday, after the release of a report accusing him of sexually harassing a female staffer, among other ethics violations. New Jersey’s governor, Mikie Sherrill, announced on Friday afternoon that Caldwell had submitted his resignation to her earlier in the day. The decision by Caldwell, 66, came one day after Sherrill called on him to step down after an investigation determined he violated state ethics rules and engaged in behavior that constituted sexual harassment. New Jersey datacenter fined $1.1m after visual investigation showed dozens of unpermitted generators Read more The 61-page report said it found credible evidence that Caldwell made romantic advances toward a female staffer’s friend, tried to secure a promotion for his girlfriend and gave tickets to personal guests without reimbursement. The New Jersey Globe was the first to report on Caldwell’s resignation. Thomas Calcagni, a lawyer for Caldwell, said in a statement they would “continue to forcefully challenge the report”. “Dr Caldwell’s resignation, submitted to put an end to the targeted campaign to discredit his character, does not in any way diminish our outrage concerning the investigative process and its specious findings,” Calcagni said. “Counsel is fully exploring all legal remedies to ensure a true, balanced, and unbiased record.” Sherrill, a Democrat, said she would appoint the state’s acting comptroller, Shirley Emehelu, as the acting lieutenant governor. “We can no longer tolerate the culture of silence, sweeping things under the rug or kicking cans down the road,” Sherrill said Friday at press conference in Trenton, the state capital. “New Jerseyans deserve fairness and they deserve accountability.” The change-up comes just weeks before midterm elections, which the lieutenant governor is responsible for overseeing. The New Jersey governor initiated an investigation into Caldwell in May after receiving an anonymous letter that accused him of “bringing uninvited female guests to events while traveling using taxpayer funds” and “hitting on women at functions”. Ultimately, investigators concluded that aspects of the allegations were credible. In one instance, investigators said Caldwell made a romantic advance toward a female staffer’s friend and then made a “derogatory or demeaning reference” about women after his advances were rebuffed. Caldwell allegedly told the staffer that women like them were ambitious and successful and needed a man in a position to help them, “but you young women are looking for young sperm”. Investigators also found that Caldwell advocated for the promotion of his girlfriend, a state employee, to a “senior leadership position”. Caldwell acknowledged that he did not disclose the nature of his relationship with the state employee until he was confronted. Caldwell had pushed for his girlfriend’s promotion, even after being informed he was under investigation. Ultimately, she did not get the promotion and no longer works in state government. Credible evidence also determined Caldwell brought at least three personal guests, including his girlfriend, to ticketed events, in his capacity as lieutenant governor, without advance authorization or payment. After Sherrill announced the report’s findings and called for Caldwell to resign, it was unclear whether or not he would step down. As lieutenant governor, Caldwell was also serving as New Jersey’s secretary of state, who is the chief elections officer. With just 39 days until the midterm elections, Sherrill said she was tapping Emehelu to ensure “all eligible New Jerseyans can make their voices heard”. “Shirley is a veteran of the US Department of Justice and the New Jersey attorney general’s office. She has the judgment to run these elections and the strength to stand up to Trump’s attacks on voting,” Sherrill added. Sherrill has 45 days to name a permanent replacement for Caldwell. https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/thomas-tu.text: Arthur Ferridge Sun, September 27, 2026 at 6:25 PM UTC 0 Thomas Tuchel has admitted he may be forced to rotate Harry Kane out of his England team as they face four matches in 11 days this international break. The Three Lions opened their Nations League campaign with a hectic 3-2 defeat by Spain on Saturday night . The result puts extra pressure on their three remaining matches in this break, with two matches against Czechia and a third against Croatia still to come. Kane started at Wembley and scored before the break, but struck a second-half penalty off the crossbar to prompt a swing in the match’s momentum. Tuchel has thrown his support behind his captain despite that miss, though, saying Kane is “desperate to start all four” games in this run, but the intense period of matches brings an extra focus on players’ fitness. “I would love not to rotate, to be honest,” Tuchel said. “I am not sure if it’s possible. “My ideal scenario would be to go again and go again and go again, with six or seven players minimum from that start again that we trust. “To put the responsibility on them and let them feel the trust. But I am not sure it’s possible. Let’s see.” Tuchel says he does not take phone calls from Premier League managers over his players, saying it is “just impossible” to manage game-time as England have to rack up wins and stay focused. “We need to be proactive and go for it,” he said of the trip to Prague. “There is no room for managing or an economic style. “It’s how the team want to play, how we want to play so let’s go.
